provenance.brief: Name a famous NBA play-by-play call, catchphrase or commentator line that fans still repeat.

Bang!.reason: Mike Breen's widely documented signature call for big made shots.

Is this the dagger?.reason: Kevin Harlan said this during Kawhi Leonard's series-winning shot against Philadelphia in Game 7 in 2019.

With no regard for human life!.reason: Kevin Harlan used this famous call for LeBron James's dunk against Boston in the 2008 playoffs.

Mama, there goes that man!.reason: A well-documented recurring Mark Jackson catchphrase during NBA broadcasts.

Hand down, man down.reason: Mark Jackson regularly used this phrase when discussing shots made against insufficient defensive contests.

Yes!.reason: Marv Albert's emphatic 'Yes!' was his signature basket call.

Havlicek stole the ball!.reason: Johnny Most's famous radio call of John Havlicek's decisive steal in the 1965 Eastern Division finals.

Bingo!.reason: Ralph Lawler's signature call for made Clippers three-pointers.

Oh me, oh my!.reason: A widely documented Ralph Lawler catchphrase from Clippers broadcasts.

Right between the eyes!.reason: Kevin Harlan has repeatedly used this phrase for made jump shots in NBA broadcasts.

Blocked by James!.reason: Mike Breen's famous call of LeBron James's block on Andre Iguodala in Game 7 of the 2016 Finals.

A steal by Bird!.reason: Johnny Most made this call during Larry Bird's pivotal steal against Detroit in Game 5 of the 1987 Eastern Conference finals.

A spectacular move!.reason: Marv Albert used this call for Michael Jordan's switching-hands layup in Game 2 of the 1991 Finals.

Gimme the hot sauce!.reason: A documented Stacey King catchphrase celebrating made three-pointers on Bulls broadcasts.

First to 100 wins.reason: Ralph Lawler regularly invoked Lawler's Law: the first team to 100 points wins.

Too big, too strong, too fast, too good.reason: Stacey King used this well-known sequence to celebrate Derrick Rose's play on Bulls broadcasts.
